fields.required_evidence: Set of distinct Stark v9.3.0 levels; DONE needs one evidence record per listed level.
fields.slices: Single-PR slices of at most 10 h. Required before IN_PROGRESS for any ticket over 12 h.
fields.validation_hours: Opus validation budget (separate session from the implementer).
fields.external_blocker: {owner (role, never a guessed person), unblock_step, needed_by, raised_on}; days waiting = today - raised_on while unresolved.
fields.due: Hard date for gate tickets; other tickets follow their wave window in PLAN.md.

tickets.title: Establish the release evidence chain and readiness labels (ADR-017) and make the ledger reject closure without evidence
tickets.summary: False closure is the program's biggest risk (ChatGPT audit section 5): persuasive reports and green unit tests are not packaged-product proof. Define one immutable evidence record per level per ticket linking requirement or defect, reproduction, commit, artifact hash, environment, executed test, result, implementer and validator, and a checker that computes closure from those records. It also fixes the dependency rule: artifact dependencies cap closure, decision dependencies do not (work proceeds on the recorded default, labelled ASSUMED).
acceptance: JSON schema for evidence records: ticket, evidence_level, per-kit_ref status (MET/PARTIAL/BLOCKED/NOT_MET), finding_refs, repro, commit, artifact_sha256 (packaged), environment and host identity, command, exit_code, result, ci_run_id, implementer_session, validator_session, inherited_block; one record file per ticket under docs/metis-2.0/evidence/records/

Status vocabulary TODO/IN_PROGRESS/ENGINEERING_COMPLETE/BLOCKED_EXTERNAL/DEFERRED/DONE/CANCELLED documented in docs/metis-2.0/README.md; DEFERRED means shipped flag-off with a recorded owner approval under the degrade order (D-14)

Dependency semantics in the README: depends_on lists artifact dependencies; a ticket enters the ready queue when each is ENGINEERING_COMPLETE, DONE, DEFERRED or BLOCKED_EXTERNAL; while an artifact dependency is BLOCKED_EXTERNAL the downstream ticket can close only as ENGINEERING_COMPLETE, its records carry inherited_block, and it becomes DONE when the upstream is DONE and the affected verification is re-run. needs_decision lists D-x decisions: work proceeds on the recorded default labelled ASSUMED, is never capped by the decision, and is re-validated if the recorded answer differs (the check lists those tickets)

required_evidence is a set of Stark v9.3.0 levels, which are distinct and unordered (DESIGNED, LOCALLY_TESTED, HOST_CONFIGURED, LIVE_VERIFIED, ACCEPTED, MEASURED); scripts/evidence/check.mjs requires one record per listed level before DONE and rejects any other level value

LOCALLY_TESTED needs a CI run ID on the PR head SHA; LIVE_VERIFIED needs harness-produced suite or census output plus the artifact sha256 from the build lane (M2-0187) and the host identity, never prose; MEASURED needs the raw measurement file; ACCEPTED needs the owner's dated statement
Fix tickets carry red-before (the new test fails on the parent commit) and green-after runs, both recorded

'Wired for real' is defined and checked: a real client code path with no production stub, a schema-faithful contract fake used only in tests, a one-command live probe script, and BLOCKED with the unblock step visible in the in-app capability matrix; anything less is NOT_MET
implementer_session must differ from validator_session (a reviewer never approves its own work); the PR template requires the evidence record path and the reviewing model
check.mjs refuses IN_PROGRESS for a ticket over 12 h without slices of at most 10 h
scripts/evidence/sample.mjs draws a random 10% of tickets closed since the previous gate for re-execution by a different model; results are recorded as evidence with reexecuted_by

Exception by definition of done: the program sign-off (M2-0184) may be DONE with inherited blocks, because the goal defines done as engineering-complete with every external dependency BLOCKED and visible; its record lists each inherited block with its unblock step

tickets.title: Stop foreign-key and keystore failures from quarantining the brain index: ownership stamp plus decrypt-failure taxonomy
tickets.summary: quarantineUnusableIndex renames any index.json that fails to decrypt, so a process holding a different key (a test worker, another device on a shared .brain) resets the owner's ledger and forces a full re-ingest, which feeds the heavy-machine loop. Stamp a plaintext index.owner.json with the existing installId on every successful writeIndex, and classify decrypt failures as unparseable, foreign-key or keystore-unavailable. Only an unparseable index owned by this install (or unowned, for backward compatibility) is quarantined; everything else stays byte-identical and opens read-only for the session.
acceptance: writeIndex stamps .brain/index.owner.json {installId, updatedAt} (no content) after each successful write
Foreign installId or keystore-unavailable leaves index.json byte-identical, returns an in-memory empty read-only index and audits brain.ledger.foreign_key (content-free)
Own or unowned plus unparseable keeps today's rename behaviour; new quarantine snapshots are capped at 5; the existing 180 index.corrupt-* files are never deleted by the app
Correlation note records quarantine timestamps against known test-run windows (metadata only, owner-approved) to close CRITIC-INV-2
Three ownership cases plus the backward-compatible case are covered in mqa-175-brain-index-poison.test.ts

When the ledger opens read-only (foreign-key or keystore-unavailable), the index is flagged unavailable so the scheduler suspends backfill, ingest, consolidation and the intelligence catch-up (deferredReason ledger_unavailable) instead of re-extracting every meeting against the empty in-memory index; data health shows the state

Two-device case: a .brain shared by two installs flips the owner stamp; a test proves neither device quarantines or re-ingests, and the remaining risk is stated as a 1.9.7 residual until the ledger moves to userData (M2-0205)
verification: npx vitest run src/main/mqa-175-brain-index-poison.test.ts src/main/brain/store.test.ts
Fixture: an index encrypted with a foreign key is byte-identical (sha256) after readIndex()

tickets.title: Make model choice an Operator-managed fleet policy: the owner picks models per capability in the portal and every Métis app enforces it
tickets.summary: Owner requirement (2026-09-28, OD-18): 'I decide what model on the portal and every Métis app abides by that.' Today model choice is local: each app reads its own settings (src/shared/ipc.ts BaseSettingsSchema provider default 'cloudflare') plus an optional admin-managed config file (src/main/store.ts allowedProviders, readTrustedAdminManaged). The Operator portal brokers asks (operatorAskTransport in src/main/import-recap.ts) and has settings-store / seat routes, but there is no portal page that sets models and no fleet policy the apps fetch and obey. Build one owner-controlled model policy, served by the Operator, enforced by the Electron app on macOS and Windows and by the native Mac app.
acceptance: Operator portal 'Models' page (owner role only): pick the provider + model per capability — ask/chat, command agent, meeting recap/extraction, STT, TTS, embeddings, local model — plus allowed fallbacks; every change is versioned and audited (who, when, old -> new).

The Operator serves the policy as a signed, versioned document on a device-authenticated endpoint (use the existing seat / desktop-license device authentication now; switch to M2-0145's per-device HMAC binding when it lands). Every app verifies the signature before use; a tampered or unsigned policy is rejected with an audit event.

Electron app (macOS + Windows) and native Mac app fetch the policy at start and on change (push or poll <= 60 s), cache the last valid signed policy for offline use, and route every model call through it — the local settings cannot select a model outside the policy (Settings shows the policy's choice as managed/locked with the portal as the source).
Operator-brokered calls enforce the same policy server-side: a request naming a model the policy does not allow is refused (typed error), so an old or modified client cannot bypass it.
Precedence is defined and tested: owner portal policy > MDM admin-managed file allowedProviders (can only narrow) > user settings; no policy yet = today's defaults with a visible 'not managed' state.

Tests: Operator route + signature tests (vitest), desktop policy client tests (fetch, verify, cache, offline, change applied without restart), a contract test that every model call site resolves through the policy module, native Mac unit tests (Swift, CI), and a packaged-smoke row POLICY-01 on macOS + Windows: change the policy on a test Operator, the running app switches model within 60 s.
verification: CI Build & Test on the PR
Operator Worker tests
per-PR packaged smoke (macOS + Windows) row POLICY-01
tickets.notes: 2026-09-28 (lead): no hard dependency on M2-0145/M2-0103 — build and prove in CI (Operator Worker tests + desktop + packaged smoke against a test Operator); production deploy of the Operator stays an owner action.
